text: Lesson 30 left you with three stubs and one open question: how does a single class support plain server calls and a client-callable entry point at the same time. This lesson answers that and finishes implementing every method.

TaskUtils now extends AbstractAjaxProcessor, the same base class Chapter 4 used. isUserInGroup's real logic first guards against an empty user ID or group name, returning false immediately. Then it looks up the group by name - if no group exists with that name, it returns false right there. Only if the group is found does it query sys_user_grmember for a matching membership record, using setLimit(1) so the query stops at the first match instead of scanning further, exactly the performance discipline Chapter 3 taught.

Right alongside it sits ajaxIsUserInGroup - a thin wrapper with no real parameters of its own. It pulls the user ID and group name out of this.getParameter, the exact pattern from Chapter 4, then calls the real isUserInGroup method and converts the result to a string with toString. Only this wrapper method needs the Client callable checkbox checked - isUserInGroup itself does not.

Here's a Client Script calling it, the way Chapter 4's GlideAjax lesson taught. It builds a GlideAjax request naming TaskUtils and ajaxIsUserInGroup, adds the user ID and group name as parameters, and checks the answer that comes back. GlideAjax always returns its answer as text, never as a native boolean, so the comparison is written as answer strictly equal to the string true, not a loose comparison.

formatDueDate takes a GlideDateTime object, not a raw string. It first checks for an empty date using getNumericValue equal to zero, which catches a GlideDateTime that exists but was never given a real value. Then it uses GlideDateTime's own before method to compare against right now, appending the word overdue to the display string when the due date has already passed. getReferenceDisplayValue checks isValidField before calling getDisplayValue, so a typo'd field name logs a clear message and returns an empty string instead of breaking.

Three stubs are now three real, working methods. isUserInGroup works from both the server and the client. formatDueDate handles overdue dates correctly using Chapter 2's date comparison tools. getReferenceDisplayValue never returns null, and never crashes on a bad field name.

The class works. Next up: Lesson 32 reviews this code the way a senior developer would before anyone else relies on it - checking for performance pitfalls, correct equality checks, and sensible logging.
